title: Retrospective study on morphological brain changes in former preterm infants following unilateral periventricular hemorrhagic infarction
summary:
Infants born prematurely before 32 weeks of gestation often suffer brain damage and developmental impairments. While the extent and frequency of some forms of such brain damage are well characterized, there is insufficient information available regarding other types of damage—particularly underdevelopment of the cerebellum, which may not become apparent until later in life.
Therefore, this study aims to investigate the frequency and extent of damage to the cerebellum and other brain structures resulting from intraventricular hemorrhage grade II or higher and additional hemorrhage into the adjacent brain tissue in preterm infants born before 32 weeks of gestation who were treated at the Neonatal Center at the Hegau -Bodensee-Klinikum Singen from 2008 to 2024 and who subsequently underwent magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) of the head.
The primary outcome measure is underdevelopment of the side of the cerebellum opposite the side of the brain where hemorrhage into the brain tissue was detected during the neonatal period. It is hypothesized that underdevelopment occurs in the majority of patients and is more pronounced than previously described. Secondary outcome measures include atrophy of other brain structures. The study will also examine cases of isolated intraventricular hemorrhage without hemorrhage in the adjacent brain tissue, as in such cases, minimal or no underdevelopment of the cerebellum and other brain structures is expected.
conditions: Intracerebral (nontraumatic) haemorrhage of fetus and newborn

interventions.name: Study arm 1 consists of former preterm infants born before 32 weeks of gestation between 2008 and 2024 who suffered intraventricular hemorrhage and periventricular hemorrhagic infarction (PVHI) during the first weeks of life and later underwent a cranial MRI (cMRI). This cMRI will be evaluated.

Study arm 2 consists of former preterm infants born before 32 weeks of gestation between 2008 and 2024 who suffered an isolated intraventricular hemorrhage during the first weeks of life and later underwent a cMRI. The results of this cMRI will be evaluated.

As a control group, we will use cMRI images from 20 patients that were obtained from neurologically healthy children due to other medical conditions (e.g., in the ear, nose, and throat or ophthalmological fields)

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Study participants: Former preterm infants born before 32 weeks of gestation between 2008 and 2024 who suffered intraventricular hemorrhage of grade II or higher during the first weeks of life and later underwent a cranial MRI (cMRI).
Control group: Children who are neurologically healthy and who underwent head MRI scans due to other medical conditions (e.g., in the ear, nose, and throat or ophthalmological fields).
Exclusion criteria:
Children with chromosomal abnormalities or cerebral malformations
